title.narrative: Vaccin University of Rwanda, EU-delegering MAV+ och vaccinacceptans
Vaccines University of Rwanda, EU-Delegation MAV+, and vaccine uptake

description.narrative: Contributions to strengthen capacity for vaccine development and production in Rwanda. The main contribution is the implementation of the EU's Global Gateway program Team Europe Initiative "MAV+" with the objective of strengthening capacity for vaccine development and production in Rwanda, in collaboration with the University of Rwanda and three Swedish universities, as well as a smaller program with the University of Rwanda for vaccine acceptance research.

Insatser för att stärka kapaciteten för vaccinutveckling och produktion i Rwanda. Inom ramen för insatserna ingår genomförandet av EU's Global Gateway-program Team Europe Initiative "MAV+" med målsättningen att stärka kapacitet för vaccinutveckling och produktion i Rwanda, i samarbete med University of Rwanda och tre svenska universitet, samt en mindre insats med University of Rwanda för forskning om vaccinacceptans.

Rwanda is leading efforts to transform Africas vaccine manufacturing capacity. Significant progress has been made in building infrastructure, such as Africas first mRNA vaccine manufacturing facility (BioNTech), and strengthening regulatory frameworks, including reaching WHO Maturity Level 3 of the national medical agency (RDFA) and the hosting the African Medical Agency (AMA). However, critical gaps remain in research capacity and clinical trial site development. Sweden, with its expertise in global health, research, and capacity strengthening, is uniquely positioned to support Rwanda in these areas. Targeted investments in research, workforce training, and clinical trial site improvement will complement ongoing donor efforts focused on manufacturing and regulatory strengthening, also part of the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) Manufacturing and Access to Vaccines, Medicines, and Health Technology Products in Africa (MAV). This holistic approach will ensure that vaccines produced in Rwanda meet international standards and address top priority diseases of the continent. Sida's contribution will be implemented by University of Rwanda (UR) in close cooperation with three Swedish universities (Karolinska Institutet, Göteborg university and Umeå University. The interventions long-term goal is that Rwanda makes an important contribution to the development and manufacturing of Africas needs of vaccines, medicines and health technologies. Rwanda and Africa at large have a severe shortage of human resources for health, science, and technology. This human resource gap creates a limitation for Rwanda to use and adapt emerging technologies that would have the potential to improve quality of life for Rwandan people, drive socio-economic development and foster sustainable growth. Objectives of the intervention The overall program objective is Strengthened environment for local pharmaceutical and health technologies production through research, higher education and professional skills development in Rwanda, with the following specific objectives: - To strengthen the capacity of the University of Rwanda to conduct high-quality in-country research and professional training; - To increase the number of skilled workforces in health and life-sciences; - To strengthen in-country capacity to conduct clinical trials. By the end of the intervention, we expect to see 6 new MSc programs and a One PhD program developed and implemented, 100 MSc and 13 PhD graduates and 3 postdocs. We expect more than 60 new peer-reviewed research publications. 2 clinical trial sites are expected to be certified and 5 to be upgraded in their quality management systems, and at least 5 cohorts of clinical trial staff to have been trained.
This is a new contribution (from March 2025) and results will be published later.
